srs_fr016_minting_decision.question: Is DSHN-70's gap (DPDP erasure never reaching Zone 3/Zone 5 data) already covered by SRS.md's existing NFR-006/AC-013, or does it need a new FR-016?

text_read.nfr_006: SRS.md: 'The system SHALL support DPDP Act 2023 (India) compliance for any zone that stores PII extracted from conversations, including purpose-limitation and data-subject rights (erasure) support.' (High priority) - this is deliberately zone-agnostic: 'any zone that stores PII', not an enumerated subset.
text_read.ac_013: SRS.md: 'Given a data subject requests erasure, When the erasure cascade executes across all 8 zones plus indices and archives, Then the subject's payload content becomes permanently unrecoverable via crypto-shredding while the Zone 7 provenance chain structure... remains intact and verifiable.' - explicitly 'across all 8 zones', not a subset.
text_read.ac_013_section_4_1: SRS.md's own 2026-09-19 append-only correction (Section 4.1, added at v1.0.9, DSHN-60 remediation) already states plainly: 'AC-013 is not yet met by the shipped code... Closing AC-013 itself remains open work.' It further scopes what was actually shipped as 'item_id-keyed... covering Zone 6... and Zone 2... not all 8 zones, not Zone 8 archives.' This note predates DSHN-70's own finding (2026-09-20) but already anticipated the same shape of gap for Zone 2/6 specifically, and states the crypto-shredding mechanism itself does not exist anywhere in the codebase.

srs_fr016_minting_decision.decision: NO new FR-016 is minted by this file. NFR-006 and AC-013 already cover DSHN-70's gap textually and completely: NFR-006's 'any zone that stores PII' and AC-013's 'across all 8 zones' already require exactly what DSHN-70 finds missing (Zone 3/Zone 5 reach). DSHN-70 is not a new requirement discovery the way FR-013 was in SRS.md's own v1.0.6 Change Log entry - FR-013 was minted because SRS.md's FR table genuinely had no row at all for the Zone 3/5 conflict-detection-sweep requirement (three other artifacts already referenced 'FR-013' as adopted before the FR table itself caught up - a real docs-drift gap in the requirement's existence). DSHN-70, by contrast, is an implementation-completeness gap against a requirement (AC-013) that already exists, is already explicitly scoped to 'all 8 zones', and is already explicitly logged in SRS.md's own Section 4.1 as 'not yet met'. Minting FR-016 here would create a second, duplicate requirement for the exact same obligation AC-013 already states, diluting rather than clarifying SRS.md's Change Log discipline.
srs_fr016_minting_decision.justification_pattern_followed: This mirrors SRS.md's own v1.0.6 Change Log entry's reasoning in reverse: that entry minted FR-013 because openapi.yaml/integration-testing-plan.md/rtm-async-workers.md already referenced FR-013 as adopted while the FR table had literally no corresponding row - a requirement-existence gap. Here, the requirement (AC-013/NFR-006) already exists, is already correctly scoped, and its own non-fulfillment is already disclosed in the SRS itself (Section 4.1). The correct action, per SRS.md's own append-only Change Log convention (rules/44-srs-lifecycle.md Section 4.3), is a new dated Change Log row noting DSHN-70 as further evidence against the already-open AC-013 gap - not a new FR.
srs_fr016_minting_decision.action_taken: No edit was made to SRS.md by this file (out of this task's scope: it asked for a routing-index JSON, not an SRS edit). This decision is recorded here so the eventual SRS.md update (when FR-013's wiring gap and DSHN-70's erasure-scope gap are actually closed) can cite this file's reasoning rather than independently re-deciding whether FR-016 is needed.
